Royal Mail FDS - Processing Sites: Worked Example

section.simpara: Royal Mail operates a national network of Processing Sites - Mail Centres, RDCs, Hubs and Super Hubs, International, through which all letter and parcel volumes are sorted, consolidated, and dispatched. Workforce planning across this estate has historically relied on a combination of MDS (Master Duty System), spreadsheet-based duty rosters, and locally held overtime sign-off processes. This fragmentation creates discrepancies between planned hours, scanned attendance, and paid hours in PSP, with downstream consequences for cost recognition, finance reporting, and audit assurance.

The Front Line Demand and Supply (FDS) application already deployed for Delivery Offices is being extended to Processing Sites to provide a single, integrated, auditable workforce-planning platform across the frontline estate. The MVP scope is defined in the Processing - High Level Requirements artefact (story IDs MDS_MVP01_01 through MDS_MVP24_01).

simpara.emphasis: Capabilities delivered by FDS at Processing Sites:

entry.simpara: Structured scheduling interfaces for duty planning across delivery offices and processing sites. Consumes master duty and reference data from DDS for deliveries and MDS for Processing sites , establishing a standardised, auditable record of scheduling intent across the frontline estate.
A dedicated scheduling environment for overtime attendance across delivery offices and processing sites. Generates structured OT plans that serve as the authoritative reference for Qlik Reporting.

Cross-references the approved OT plan against real-time PDA and Console attendance scan data. Authorised personnel such as site managers, shift managers and book-room staff review and approve records for overtime payment processing via PSP.

Cross-references agency worker shift plans against PDA and Console attendance scan data. Approved records are transmitted to the JoinedUp agency payroll platform via API, eliminating manual data re-entry and accelerating cost recognition.

Reconciles planned versus actual hours across delivery offices and processing sites, disaggregated by workforce category - AWD, overtime, and agency. Generates structured data sets consumed by Royal Mail’s financial reporting infrastructure for cost governance and expenditure management.

listitem.simpara: Import Processing duty data from MDS into FDS for all Mail Centres, Parcel Hubs and Super Hubs (MDS_MVP01_01).
Allocate duty holders and rotation weeks against the imported duty data (MDS_MVP03_01–03).

entry.simpara: Every approved overtime, schedule-attendance and agency timesheet record carries a cryptographically immutable audit trail showing originating duty, scan events used for validation, approver identity and timestamp; complete trail retrievable within 5 seconds for any record over the last 7 years.

For 99.5% of approved timesheet submissions, the hours transmitted to PSP / JoinedUp match the verified PDA/Console scan-derived hours to within ±2 minutes; manual override events are logged and reportable.

FDS web UI available 99.7% of the time during the operational window 24x7, with planned maintenance windows agreed with service; degraded-mode local edit-and-resync supported for up to 2 hours of integration outage.
Inbound MDS feeds processed within 30 minutes of receipt with 100% record-level reconciliation; outbound PSP/JoinedUp/DP feeds delivered within agreed SLAs and end-to-end reconciled daily.
A trained PSM completes a full-shift attendance plan adjustment (cover absence, extend AWD to OT, re-allocate to work area) in under 90 seconds

entry.simpara: FDS is already deployed for Deliveries and Collection Points. The Processing extension must be implemented on the same platform to avoid bifurcating the front-line estate model and to leverage the existing operational, support and compliance posture.
MDS is the system of record for duty data
All duty master data (duty codes, work-area splits, rotation patterns) originates in MDS. FDS holds an operational copy refreshed monthly and on demand it does not author duty in MVP
PSP is the only payroll endpoint for AWD/OT/SA
Authorised overtime and schedule-attendance records must be submitted to PSP for payment. FDS must produce PSP-compatible records and reconcile their acceptance.
JoinedUp is the agency payroll endpoint
Approved agency timesheets must be transmitted to JoinedUp via its supported API. No bypass route is permitted.
Scan data sources are PDA and Console only
Validation of attendance hours uses only RMG-issued PDA scans and Console-recorded scans. No third-party time clocks are in scope.
Strategic reporting consumes FDS data through the enterprise Data Platform (DP) and visualises it in Qlik / Qlik Sense. Bespoke reporting solutions are not permitted.
New compute and integration components must run on the Royal Mail strategic cloud platform.
Workforce-affecting changes (rosters, OT, scan-based pay validation) must be deployable with appropriate consultation; the design must support phased site-by-site rollout.
The system must not facilitate non-compliant rest-period or maximum-hours patterns; warnings should surface at Over Time planning stage in FDS.
Personally Identifying Information (employee identifiers, scan timestamps, location) must be processed and retained in line with RMG’s data-protection schedule.
Cost-affecting flows (RCS reporting, PSP/JoinedUp submissions) require segregation of duties and immutable audit trails to meet internal-control requirements.
New integration points expose REST APIs published in the BIG APIM gateway and registered in the API catalogue.
PDA and Console scan events are ingested through existing message queues hosted in the BIG IBM MQ, no direct point-to-point coupling.
All HLDs are authored using this template, stored in the Confluence space, and reviewed by the ARB Council before build start.

Royal Mail FDS - Processing Sites: Worked Example
The FDS Processing Sites architecture is governed by five fundamental decisions:

section.title: Reuse, do not re-platform
section.simpara: FDS is extended, not rebuilt. Processing capabilities are added as additional bounded contexts within the existing FDS solution, sharing identity, audit, integration, master data and storage layers. This delivers cost containment and consistency across Delivery and Processing Units.

section.title: Data-driven planning
section.simpara: Duty masters (codes, work-area splits, rotation patterns) are owned by MDS and pulled into FDS on a monthly bulk cadence with on-demand deltas. FDS authoritatively derives plans from this master data; any operational variance is captured as a tracked, auditable adjustment rather than a redefinition of the duty. Additionally, FDS allows ad hoc overtime planning.

section.title: Plan vs. scan reconciliation as the canonical pay-validation pattern
section.simpara: Pay-affecting decisions (OT and Schedule-Attendance approval) cross-reference the approved plan against PDA and Console scan events. The plan is the authoritative reference for downstream timesheet validation; manual override is permitted but always logged.

section.title: Event-driven, API-led integration
section.simpara: High-volume, low-latency flows (scan events and PSP OT flow) use the IBM MQ. Lower-volume flows (Joined up and People app) use synchronous APIs through the BIG API gateway. Bulk analytics flows to the Data Platform use the Batch data export. No point-to-point integration is introduced.

simpara.emphasis: Software security architecture is the foundational design of a system that embeds defenses directly into the code and infrastructure, ensuring resistance against malicious attacks. It is a critical necessity to proactively mitigate vulnerabilities, prevent catastrophic data breaches, and maintain customer trust
A robust software security architecture is essential for several key reasons:

listitem.simpara: Proactive Vulnerability Mitigation: By designing security into the software development life cycle (SDLC) from the ground up, you can prevent up to 80% of security problems before the code is even written. It replaces reactive, "afterthought" patching with built-in resilience.

Minimizing Breach Impact: A solid architecture ensures that if a component is breached, the damage is isolated. Principles like "least privilege" and strict access controls prevent an attacker from escalating their access across the entire system.
Protecting Critical Assets: It establishes standardized encryption, authentication, and authorization checkpoints to safeguard sensitive user data, intellectual property, and financial systems.

Ensuring Compliance: For highly regulated industries like finance, healthcare, and e-commerce, a structured architectural framework is required to meet strict legal regulations and data protection laws

simpara.emphasis: The primary rationale for software security architecture is to proactively embed protective measures into a system, rather than treating them as an afterthought. It acts as a foundational blueprint that minimizes the attack surface, prevents costly architectural reworks, and ensures business-wide compliance.
The fundamental drivers and objectives of this architecture include:

listitem.simpara: Shift-Left Approach: Embedding security during the initial planning and design phases is exponentially more cost-effective than remediating vulnerabilities found in production.

Complexity Management: Modern software relies heavily on distributed systems and APIs. Security architecture provides consistent, unified controls rather than fragmented, bolt-on solutions that leave systems fragile.
Confidentiality: Ensures that sensitive data is protected from unauthorized access, leveraging end-to-end encryption and robust identity access management (IAM).
Integrity: Maintains the accuracy and trustworthiness of data by implementing strict authorization protocols and data classification policies.
Availability: Ensures services and data remain accessible, even amidst malicious disruptions or unintended software failures
Segregation & Segmentation: Hybrid and cloud environments require independent building blocks so that a compromise in one service does not cascade through the entire organization.
Zero-Trust Frameworks: Assumes no user or service is trusted by default. Architecture mandates continuous validation, authentication, and authorization.
Compliance: Aligns system designs with data privacy and cybersecurity laws, such as GDPR and other industry frameworks.
Cost Reduction: Minimizes long-term expenses by preventing security breaches, reducing expensive downtime, and streamlining incident response.

simpara.emphasis: Security Architecture can be documented through diagrams, text and tables. This section should contain at least a Level-1 DFD along with a STRIDE Threat Model with clearly defined threat boundaries. RAID Logs should be in tabular format.

simpara.emphasis: Data architecture is the blueprint that dictates how an organization acquires, stores, transforms, distributes, and consumes data. It provides a standardized framework that connects business objectives to technical infrastructure, ensuring data is secure, consistent, scalable, and readily accessible for operations and AI applications.
A robust data architecture consists of several interconnected building blocks:

listitem.simpara: Data Models: Blueprints that map data structures, relationships, and business rules.
Data Flow & Pipelines: Systems that ingest, process, and move data from sources to destinations.
Data Storage: The repositories where data lives, such as Data Lakes, Data Warehouses, or Lakehouses.
Data Governance & Security: Policies, standards, and access controls that maintain data quality and ensure regulatory compliance.

simpara.emphasis: A robust data architecture aligns data systems with business goals, providing a blueprint for data management, storage, and usage. Its core benefits include unified governance, improved data quality, and scalable infrastructure that accelerates real-time analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.

listitem.simpara: Eliminates Data Silos: Unifies disparate systems, allowing departments to securely share data and establish a reliable "single version of the truth".
Enhanced Data Quality: Enforces consistent data standards and validation rules to minimize duplication and prevent inaccurate reporting.
Scalability & Cost Optimization: Optimizes cloud storage and data processing, reducing hardware needs and allocating operational resources efficiently.
Unified Governance & Compliance: Implements centralized protocols to secure sensitive information and meet regulatory frameworks like GDPR.
Accelerated Innovation: Provides a reliable, controlled foundation for advanced technologies like AI, machine learning, and real-time predictive analytics.

simpara.emphasis: In modern data platforms, the "Raw → Curated → Consumption" pipeline is a standardized approach to data organization, often referred to as the Medallion Architecture (Bronze → Silver → Gold). It ensures data integrity, minimizes pipeline fragility, and optimizes information for downstream analytics and machine learning.

listitem.simpara: Raw Layer (Landing/Bronze): The Raw layer is the initial entry point where ingested data from various sources (APIs, IoT, databases, logs) is stored in its native, unaltered format.Purpose: Acts as an immutable historical record and a source of truth that allows you to replay pipelines if errors occur downstream.Data State: Unprocessed, varying structures, frequently stored as JSON, CSV, or raw binary.Who interacts: Primarily used by data engineers.

Curated Layer (Cleansed/Silver): The Curated layer sits between the raw and consumption layers, where raw data is transformed into validated, cleansed, and standardized datasets.Purpose: Establishes data reliability by removing duplicates, enforcing schema definitions, and applying business logic.Data State: Relational, standardized, and often partitioned into columnar formats like Parquet or Delta for better compression and query speed.Who interacts: Heavily accessed by data scientists and data analysts.

Consumption Layer (Serving/Gold): The Consumption layer is the final destination, engineered specifically for business users, executives, and downstream applications.Purpose: Houses highly aggregated, project-specific data ready for business intelligence (BI) reporting, dashboards, and machine learning models.Data State: Denormalized, heavily structured (often into Star or Snowflake schemas), and read-optimized.Who interacts: Business analysts, executives, and client-facing applications.

Royal Mail FDS - Processing Sites: Worked Example

section.title: Identity, Authentication and Authorisation
section.simpara: Authentication is delegated to Royal Mail AD via SAML; authorisation is enforced through AD groups including Planner-<of Location>, Approver-<of Location>, Book-room-<of Location>.

section.title: Audit and Traceability
section.simpara: An append-only audit store retains every state-changing action: plan amendments, OT/SA approvals, agency-timesheet submissions, and manual overrides. Each record carries actor identity, timestamp, source data references (scan event IDs, plan IDs). Retention is seven years, aligned with audit requirements.

section.title: Integration Resilience
section.simpara: All outbound integrations are idempotent and replayable. PSP and JoinedUp submissions use opaque idempotency keys derived from (employee, shift, approval-version).Dead-letter queues are monitored with alert thresholds.

section.title: Data Privacy and Retention
section.simpara: Personal data minimisation: only employee identifiers required for plan/scan/pay reconciliation are processed; names and full personal records remain in source systems. Retention schedules align with the RMG data-protection policy (7 years of archived data, 1 year of live data). Subject-access requests are serviceable through a support request.

section.title: Logging, Monitoring and Observability
section.simpara: Structured JSON logs, application metrics and distributed traces are emitted from every component and forwarded to the central observability platform. Service-level objectives (SLOs) for each capability are published; alerting is keyed off SLO burn rates rather than raw error counts. Operational dashboards expose plan-vs-scan reconciliation health, payroll backlog, and integration error rates.

section.title: User-experience consistency across the merged web app shell
section.simpara: The merger of the Deliveries and Processing shells (MDS_MVP16_01) is designed to be invisible to users: a single navigation, a single notification model, and a single search. Per-capability screens follow the existing Delivery patterns to minimise re-training cost for users moving between domains.

section.title: ADR-001 - Reuse the existing FDS platform rather than build a new Processing system

entry.simpara: Processing-site workforce planning needs a single, integrated, auditable platform. A net-new build would duplicate identity, audit, integration and reporting layers already proven in FDS for Deliveries.
Extend FDS; add Processing as additional bounded contexts within the existing solution.
+ Faster delivery, lower TCO, consistency across front line planning. Increased coupling within the FDS solution; mitigated by clear bounded contexts and a published internal API contract.

section.title: ADR-002 - Merge the Deliveries and Processing SISO experiences

entry.simpara: The current technical limitation prevents a user with Deliveries SISO access from also using Processing SISO (MDS_MVP16_01). This blocks shared-services users (e.g. cross-domain managers).
Implement a single web shell hosting both domains, governed by role-based authorisation.
Removes the limitation; simpler user model.

section.title: ADR-003 - MDS remains the system of record for duty data

entry.simpara: Authoring duty masters in two systems would create reconciliation problems and dilute the audit trail.
FDS holds an operational copy of MDS-owned duty data, refreshed monthly with on-demand deltas; FDS does not author duty masters.
+ Single source of truth, simpler reconciliation. Latency between MDS amendment and FDS visibility; mitigated by on-demand refresh

section.title: ADR-004 - Duty-data viewing in FDS for MVP (MDS_MVP02_01/02)

entry.simpara: PSMs can view duty data in FDS
FDS provides daily attendance plan screen for PSP to view and adjust the daily attendance plan for the processing site
Sleeker planning solution available for the processing sites

section.title: ADR-005 - Enforce idempotency on all payroll-bound submissions

entry.simpara: Duplicate payroll postings have direct financial and reputational consequences.
Every PSP and JoinedUp submission carries a deterministic idempotency key; the receiver-side or our outbound adapter rejects duplicates.
+ Pay accuracy protected during retries and outages.

simpara.emphasis: Quality scenarios make quality requirements concrete and allow to decide whether they are fulfilled (in the sense of acceptance criteria). Ensure that your scenarios are specific and measurable.

This section is complementary to NFRs defined in LeanIX. This provides an acceptance criteria for each NFR that could be tested. The distinction between an NFR and Quality Scenarios could be understood with the following examples:

informalexample.simpara: NFR – All PII data should be encrypted at rest
Quality Scenario – All PII data should be encrypted using AES256 before storing in the database.
In the above example – Just by looking at the NFR alone, we cannot test it but the associated quality scenario makes it testable
NFR – All save operations should be complete in less than 5 seconds
Quality Scenario – Upon clicking on Save button on employee edit screen, record should be saved within 3 seconds and success message should be displayed on the screen.

simpara.emphasis: Key point here is “measurable”. We can link either LeanIX or any other form of document(s) where these quality scenarios are captured.
Two kinds of scenarios are especially useful:

(also called application scenarios or use case scenarios) describe the system’s runtime reaction to a certain stimulus. This also includes scenarios that describe the system’s efficiency or performance. Example: The system reacts to a user’s request within one second.

describe the desired effect of a modification or extension of the system or of its immediate environment. Example: Additional functionality is implemented or requirements for a quality attribute change, and the effort or duration of the change is measured.
Typical information for detailed scenarios include the following:
In short form (favoured in the Q42 model):

listitem.simpara: Context/Background: What kind of system or component, what is the envirionment or situation?
Source/Stimulus: Who or what initiates or triggers a behaviour, reaction or action.
Metric/Acceptance Criteria: A response including a measure or metric.

simpara.emphasis: The long form of scenarios (favoured by the SEI and [Bass+21]) is more detailed and includes the following information:

listitem.simpara: Scenario ID: A unique identifier for the scenario.
Scenario Name: A short, descriptive name for the scenario.
Source: The entity (user, system, or event) that initiates the scenario.
Stimulus: The triggering event or condition the system must address.
Environment: The operational context or condition under which the system experiences the stimulus.
Artifact: The building-blocks or other elements of the system affected by the stimulus.
Response: The outcome or behavior the system exhibits in reaction to the stimulus.
Response Measure: The criteria or metric by which the system’s response is evaluated.
